# Jubilees Chapter 7 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

---

## 7:4 — Subject of the sin: Canaan vs. Ham

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "Canaan saw that I was in liquor and he came and took hold of me" (first person — Noah speaking) | Literal Ge'ez; first-person narrator |
| LOGOS | "Canaan saw that his grandfather was drunk. He came and laid hold of him" | Third person, clarifies "grandfather" |
| PNEUMA | "his grandson Canaan saw that he was drunk. Canaan came over, grabbed him" | Third person, adds "grandson" for clarity |

**SOPHIA:** Adopted LOGOS. The shift to third person clarifies the narrative flow. Adding "grandfather" (LOGOS) or "grandson" (PNEUMA) both work — LOGOS' "grandfather" from Canaan's perspective is slightly more elegant. The Jubilees distinction from Gen 9 (Canaan as the perpetrator, not Ham) is preserved in all three.

---

## 7:7 — "cursed his son" — Ham vs. Canaan

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "he cursed his son and said: 'Cursed be Canaan'" | "His son" = Canaan (grandson of Noah) |
| LOGOS | "he cursed his son and said: 'Cursed be Canaan'" | Same |
| PNEUMA | "He cursed him: 'Cursed be Canaan'" | "Him" is less precise |

**SOPHIA:** Adopted LOGOS/EMET (identical). "His son" here refers to Canaan as Noah's grandson/son-figure; retaining "son" follows the Ge'ez and preserves the generational ambiguity. PNEUMA's "him" loses the relational term.

---

## 7:13 — Enoch's superiority to Noah

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "he excelled the children of men save Enoch because of the righteousness wherein he was perfect" | Full literal |
| LOGOS | "he excelled all the children of men except Enoch, because of the righteousness in which he was perfect" | Same content, cleaner |
| PNEUMA | "Only Enoch surpassed Noah in righteousness" | Inverts and compresses |

**SOPHIA:** Adopted LOGOS. The formulation "he excelled... except Enoch, because of righteousness in which he was perfect" is the Jubilees statement about Noah's status. PNEUMA's inversion is accurate but restructures the emphasis.

---

## 7:16 — Kainam's sin: "sinned owing to it" vs. "corrupted him"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "he transcribed it and sinned owing to it" | Literal; "sinned owing to it" |
| LOGOS | "he transcribed it, and sinned because of it" | Same, cleaner |
| PNEUMA | "he copied it down — and it corrupted him" | Active: the text corrupts Kainam |

**SOPHIA:** Adopted LOGOS. "Sinned because of it" is the standard rendering; the sin is Kainam's own act, not something the text does to him. PNEUMA's "corrupted him" shifts moral agency away from Kainam.

---

## 7:25 — Geographic description of Shem's territory

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | Full literal with Ge'ez place-names and directional language | Preserves all detail |
| LOGOS | Preserves all place-names; light restructuring of directional clauses | Formal equivalence |
| PNEUMA | Same names but compressed: "running westward through that river" | Natural phrasing |

**SOPHIA:** Adopted LOGOS. The geographic boundary description in Jubilees is highly precise and should not be compressed; every directional clause matters for Jubilees' territorial theology. PNEUMA's compression loses some detail.

---

**Total disagreements: 5**
